scope: Read original 64 QA and viewed both old originals, new frames 00/01/03, hole nearest-8x panel and overlap-edge nearest-2x panel. All four new full-resolution frames were independently recomposed and measured. Inspected author script and reran into separate /tmp output; no author PNG changed.
visual_findings: The final overlap visibly retains the pale B page on top and the ochre A strip at right. The three final apertures reveal background with no doubled sliver; intermediate B apertures correctly reveal underlying A paper.
Paper texture landmarks stay fixed within each page during integer moves; independent complete-canvas recomposition confirms rather than assumes this continuity.

Compared with regenerated batch64, this solves the rigid-object continuity defect, but the flat background and hard thin seam lose the older scene lighting. The retained dark one-pixel extraction fringe is visible at the B right edge in 2x inspection.

A contains 8177 visible RGB colors and B 7687. This is a source-resolution geometry pilot with binary masks, not limited-palette native-grid pixel art. Layer colors stay identical across frames, while frame color counts legitimately change under occlusion.
The three hole intervals are 213 then 212 pixels; they need not be equal. The same geometry is preserved in each layer and every frame.
No text, marginal warning or receipt is supplied. This proves only the art-proposed hole alignment, not full N6 evidence authenticity, identity, responsibility or in-game interaction.
correction_audit: Independent alpha-mask comparison and rerun both give 2 newly opaque and 5 newly transparent B pixels. One-time authored geometry correction precedes animation. Producer corrected its early 4/6 report in README, code comment and producer/provenance records; images and manifest stayed unchanged.
failure_conditions: Any future per-frame repaint, scaling, noninteger shift or layer geometry/palette change invalidates the fixed-layer result.
Any final hole-mask mismatch or loss of the distinct lower A strip fails this pilot.
Binary alpha does not itself prove clean source extraction; visible fringe remains a cleanup limit.
A runtime/engine-ready or final native pixel-art claim would be unsupported.
